intro: The SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam held on 13 October 2026 was described across its three shifts as ranging from easy to moderate in difficulty. Unofficial figures suggest that good attempts varied from about 20–84 in shift 1, 65–87 in shift 2, and 86 candidates reported strong attempts in shift 3. Candidates noted that reasoning and general awareness sections were generally easier, while quantitative sections posed the greatest challenge. SSC normalises scores across shifts to ensure comparable results despite these variations.

faqs.q: What was the overall difficulty level of the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 13 October 2026?
faqs.a: Across the three shifts, the exam was reported as ranging from easy to moderate. Shift 1 had mixed reports of easy to moderate, while shifts 2 and 3 were generally described as moderate.

faqs.q: How many candidates reported good attempts in each shift of the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 13 October 2026?
faqs.a: Unofficially, shift 1 had good attempts reported in the range of 20–84, shift 2 reported 65–87, and shift 3 had a specific count of 86 candidates indicating strong attempts.

faqs.q: Which sections were considered the most challenging in the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 13 October 2026?
faqs.a: Quantitative sections were consistently noted as the toughest across all shifts, with candidates mentioning time pressure and complex calculations. English reading passages also caused time‑management concerns, especially in shift 2.

faqs.q: Did candidates face any time‑management issues during the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 13 October 2026?
faqs.a: Yes, time management was highlighted as a concern, particularly in the quantitative and English reading sections. Candidates reported difficulty completing all questions within the allotted time.

faqs.q: How does SSC compare scores across different shifts for the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 13 October 2026?
faqs.a: SSC normalises scores across shifts, applying a standardisation process to ensure that candidates are evaluated on a comparable basis regardless of the shift they attended.
